thread.document:
For the special participation A on HW9, I use Qwen to solve the non-coding analytical components (problems 2–5). The performance was very strong -- almost all questions were very quickly solved by directly copy-pasting the question, which had multiple parts often.



Executive Summary

Used qwen thinking, with max thinking context length (81920 tokens).

 I also noticed from other attempts that often giving the hint associated with the question (if the question has a hint) generally helps make its answer more likely to be correct, or guides it in the right direction very well.

 For Question 3 part b, I had to nudge it to give the answer regarding the new out_features value. However, after reminding it, all of its answers were correct.

 I also ignored small formatting issues, and noticed even with formatting issues (some symbols were not pasted/displayed properly), Qwen was still able to understand all the questions and provide correct solutions.

 For longer questions (such as question 6), I also thought about pasting/asking the questions in chunks, rather than the entire multi-part question at a time. However, I found that Qwen was able to answer correctly even when giving the entire question at a time.
